Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.block

Class StoragePile

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.block.StackRun<StorageStackBE>
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.block.StoragePile
All Implemented Interfaces:
StackRunItemAccess
public final class StoragePile extends StackRun<StorageStackBE>
A maximal contiguous vertical run of Storage Stacks, treated as one inventory.

Every operation on a Storage Stack resolves the pile it belongs to and acts on the whole column: deposits fill from the base upward whatever block or slot they were aimed at, the capability exposes every block's slots as one flat range, and settling consolidates, sorts and packs the entire height down. The base block's permanent flag is the pile's, and settling propagates it, so a pile that is split or joined returns to a consistent state.

An instance describes the run bounds at resolution time. Block entities cache it for the current tick, and placement or removal invalidates every affected cache immediately.

  • Method Details

    • at

      @Nullable public static StoragePile at(net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos pos)
      Resolves the pile containing pos, or null when that position holds no Storage Stack. Client-side levels never resolve a pile: the pile is server state, and reading its bounds would consult the server config.

    • columnHasRoomFor

      public static boolean columnHasRoomFor(net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos pos)
      Whether a Storage Stack may be created at pos: the contiguous column it would form, counting the runs both below and above it, must fit the configured maximum. Testing the whole resulting column rather than one neighboring pile is what stops a block placed into the gap between two piles from joining them into an over-tall one.

    • adoptNeighbourState

      public static void adoptNeighbourState(net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos pos, StorageStackBE placed)
      Gives a Storage Stack that has just been placed the mode of the pile it joins, taking it from the block below when there is one and otherwise from the block above. Placing a block beneath a permanent pile makes it the new base, so without this the pile would silently become temporary.

    • isPermanent

      public boolean isPermanent()
      Whether this pile's blocks survive being emptied. The base block's flag is authoritative.

    • insertAt

      public int insertAt(int flatSlot, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, boolean simulate)
      Puts what it can of stack into the one slot at flatSlot, growing the pile when that slot lies in the block above it.

      A pile is genuinely a bag, so unlike the two structures its automated insertion is an ordinary positional one: the slot named takes what a slot takes, and the settle scheduled behind it packs the pile down from the base on the next tick. Filling from the base is therefore still what a pile ends up doing, just a tick later than a player's own deposit does it. Answering for the slot given rather than for the pile is what makes the handler's slot range mean something: a caller that walks the range and sums what each slot accepts gets the pile's real capacity; reporting whole-pile capacity at every slot would multiply it.

      An automated insertion carries no player, so growth is checked against the loader-provided automation actor that would place the block.

      Parameters:
      simulate - when true, nothing is stored and the pile does not grow
      Returns:
      how many items were, or would be, taken from stack

    • settle

      public void settle()
      Consolidates and sorts the whole pile, writes it back from the base upward, propagates the base's permanent flag, removes empty blocks left at the top, and publishes all deferred changes.

      Slots that already hold what they should are left alone, so an edit that disturbs a few stacks resyncs a few blocks rather than the whole column. Publishing after the trim means a block that packing emptied away is never sent to clients only to be removed behind it.
